title: 1 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 6
description: Ten questions on 1 Corinthians 6: lawsuits between brothers, the saints who will judge, washed and sanctified and justified, and the body as a temple.

questions.text: In verse 1, before whom does the writer ask whether they dare go to law?
questions.explanation: He asks whether any of them dares go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints.

answers.text: Before the apostles, rather than the elders
Before the Gentiles, rather than the Jews
Before the unrighteous, rather than before the saints
Before their own families, rather than the assembly

questions.text: According to verse 2, what will the saints judge?
questions.explanation: The verse asks whether they do not know that the saints will judge the world.

answers.text: The world
Only their own assembly
The law
Nothing at all

questions.text: What does verse 3 say "we" will judge?
questions.explanation: The verse asks whether they do not know that we will judge angels.

answers.text: Kings
Prophets
The seas
Angels

questions.text: What does verse 5 ask about a wise man among them?
questions.explanation: The verse asks whether there is not even one wise man among them who would be able to decide between his brothers.

answers.text: Whether a wise man should be paid for judging
Whether there is not even one who could decide between brothers
Whether the wisest should lead the assembly
Whether any wise man had come from another city

questions.text: What two things does verse 7 suggest instead of having lawsuits?
questions.explanation: The verse asks, "Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?"

answers.text: To be silent and to be absent
To pay and to forget
To be wronged and to be defrauded
To accuse and to be accused

questions.text: Which three things does verse 11 say happened to them?
questions.explanation: The verse says they were washed, they were sanctified, and they were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and in the Spirit of our God.

answers.text: They were washed, sanctified and justified
They were taught, tested and sent
They were called, gathered and counted
They were anointed, crowned and seated

questions.text: How does verse 12 answer the saying "All things are lawful for me"?
questions.explanation: The verse answers that not all things are expedient, and that he will not be brought under the power of anything.

answers.text: All things are therefore good
Not all things are expedient
Only food is lawful
Nothing at all is lawful

questions.text: What does verse 14 say God did, and will also do?
questions.explanation: It says that God raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by his power.

answers.text: He made the body, and will also make it new
He gave the law, and will also judge by it
He called the saints, and will also send them out
He raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up

questions.text: What does verse 19 call their body?
questions.explanation: The verse calls their body a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in them, whom they have from God.

answers.text: A temple of the Holy Spirit
A field of the Lord
A vessel of clay
A house built on sand

questions.text: According to verse 20, why are they not their own?
questions.explanation: The verse says they were bought with a price, and therefore should glorify God in body and in spirit.

answers.text: Because they were born in Corinth
Because the assembly chose them
Because they were bought with a price
Because they had taken a vow
